trust_decision.summary: TLS client decides whether a peer chain that contains a pinned CA (pinnedPeerCertSha256) is acceptable; when no verifyPeerCertByName is set it verifies the leaf against the pinned CA with DNSName = r.Config.ServerName, and an empty ServerName makes Go's x509 Verify skip the hostname check, so any leaf issued by the pinned CA is accepted.

landing_point.why: The summary names pinnedPeerCertSha256 and CA pinning; grepping it leads straight to RandCarrier.verifyPeerCert and its foundCA branch that uses r.Config.ServerName as DNSName.

fix_sites.entry_point: every TLS client dial whose streamSettings.tlsSettings has pinnedPeerCertSha256 (crypto/tls VerifyPeerCertificate callback installed at transport/internet/tls/config.go:389)
fix_sites.module_kind: core TLS config / verifier (shared library code)

fix_sites.entry_point: outbound with streamSettings.network=grpc + security=tls (grpc Dial -> getGrpcClient at transport/internet/grpc/dial.go:54,77)
outbound with streamSettings.network=hysteria + TLS (hysteria Dial, QUIC)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: transport/internet/hysteria/dialer.go:348 and transport/internet/grpc/dial.go:139-142 (each derives SNI itself instead of via tls.WithDestination; the hysteria one hands the config to quic-go, which sets ServerName on its own copy so the verifier's r.Config.ServerName stays empty)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about CA pinning in the TLS verifier; gRPC and Hysteria are separate transports that already 'set SNI' (grpc copies the domain at dial.go:140-142, quic-go fills SNI itself), so a solver can argue they are already fine and only patch verifyPeerCert, or, the other way round, add a guard in the verifier and miss that these transports never fill r.Config.ServerName for IP or QUIC dials.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pinning a LEAF hash must keep working with no serverName (early return at foundLeaf). verifyPeerCertByName together with a pinned CA must keep working. gRPC/Hysteria/realm outbounds that pin a CA with no explicit serverName must still connect to a correctly named server using the outbound address. A verifier-only 'reject empty ServerName' fix breaks the Hysteria and gRPC-over-IP cases unless the dialers pass WithDestination; rejecting all pinned-CA configs breaks legitimate use.

O6_input_shapes: serverName empty with a domain outbound address (grpc pre-fix copied it only for domains: transport/internet/grpc/dial.go:140)
serverName empty with an IP outbound address (WithDestination uses dest.Address.String(): transport/internet/tls/config.go:492)
QUIC transport where the library fills SNI on its own config copy (transport/internet/hysteria/dialer.go:348)
pinned hash matching an intermediate/CA rather than the leaf (transport/internet/tls/config.go:565-574)

O7_producer.where: transport/internet/tls/config.go:364-416 (GetTLSConfig builds the tls.Config whose ServerName the verifier later reads through r.Config, set at transport/internet/tls/config.go:391); callers then copy or clone it (transport/internet/tls/tls.go:149-160, transport/internet/tls/grpc.go:56-63, transport/internet/finalmask/realm/http.go:87-88)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: finalmask 'realm' HTTP client builds its TLS config with GetTLSConfig() and no WithDestination; net/http sets SNI on its own clone, so the verifier's r.Config.ServerName stays empty when serverName is unset. The fix did not touch it, and only the central fail-closed check covers it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: finalmask/realm is a neighbouring NAT-punch/rendezvous helper, not a proxy transport; it looks like a side channel outside 'TLS client' scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (transport/internet/finalmask/realm) from the landing point in transport/internet/tls

O8_uncovered_routes.route: RAW/TCP dial with serverName=fromMitm uses WithOverrideName(mitmServerName), which can be empty when the context carries no MITM name, leaving ServerName empty for the pinned-CA branch. The fix did not touch it, and only the central check covers it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fromMitm SNI mode is a special MITM-forwarding feature, an 'unsupported combination' with CA pinning.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: grpcUtls.ClientHandshake sets ServerName from authority on a Clone, so a verifier that reads a captured config pointer would see the pre-clone value
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The clone is already there to 'avoid clobbering ServerName'; a maintainer wiring pinning through this credentials type would naturally read the original config.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: copyConfig to utls copies ServerName by value while VerifyPeerCertificate stays bound to the original RandCarrier.Config; a dialer that sets SNI after copying gives a check/use differential
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The uTLS fingerprint path is a second TLS implementation that already copies fields by hand.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a DoQ/DoH nameserver variant that accepts user tlsSettings (with pinning) but builds the config without WithDestination
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The QUIC nameserver already builds a tls.Config ad hoc; adding user TLS settings there is a plausible feature.

O9_family: certificate validation: hostname not bound to the pinned CA (CWE-297, improper validation of certificate with host mismatch)

O10_build.project_tests: transport/internet/tls/pin_test.go:102-153 (unit tests for verifyPeerCert on leaf and CA pins; always set ServerName), testing/scenarios/tls_test.go:111 and others (end-to-end loopback TLS with PinnedPeerCertSha256), transport/internet/websocket/ws_test.go:139, transport/internet/splithttp/splithttp_test.go:148, transport/internet/httpupgrade/httpupgrade_test.go:198

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: In verifyPeerCert's foundCA branch, return an error when ServerName is empty (or verify with some fallback name), without making the gRPC/Hysteria dialers pass tls.WithDestination; or the reverse, patching only the dialers' SNI and leaving the verifier failing open for realm/fromMitm.

out_of_scope_notes: transport/internet/tls/config.go:327-329 builds an error with errors.New but never returns it (the code falls through to a generic error return, so no security effect).
transport/internet/hysteria/hub.go:221-226 masquerade proxy uses InsecureSkipVerify when masqUrlInsecure is set; this is a separate, opt-in feature.
transport/internet/reality/reality.go:76 has its own VerifyPeerCertificate, which is a different protection.
